coreIdea: Relation = subset of A×A. Core skill: check Reflexive/Symmetric/Antisymmetric/Transitive for a given rule. Equivalence = Refl+Sym+Trans. Partial Order = Refl+Antisym+Trans.
mustRememberFormulas: Largest equivalence relation = n² pairs (A×A); smallest = n pairs (identity)

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: relation defined by a formula, asked which properties hold / order type
R∪S or R∩S of two equivalence relations

commonTrapsQuickList: Symmetric ≠ opposite of Antisymmetric — test both independently
Intersection of equivalence relations is always equivalence; UNION usually is NOT
'Number of equivalence relations' (Bell number, hard) vs 'size of largest equivalence relation' (n², easy) — read carefully
'Symmetric+transitive ⟹ reflexive' proof is FLAWED for isolated elements with no related pair
highYieldPyqLessons: Property-checking (reflexive/symmetric/antisymmetric/transitive) is 16/38 PYQs — the single most important sub-skill in all of Discrete Math.
Always test small concrete examples first; abstract algebraic proof under exam time pressure is slower and error-prone.
